Subject: RFI: Dedicated GPU capacity - initial questionnaire

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this — Aurora is consolidating inference workloads for our analytics product and we're collecting detailed capacity and commitment guidance from two vendors. Attached is our baseline questionnaire (we've redacted PII). High level: we expect ~30 sustained inference requests/sec during peak windows across 4 regions, avg payload ~1.2k tokens/request, and an expected growth trajectory of ~30% Y/Y. We also need to understand burst behavior (spikes to ~150 req/s for short windows), model variants you support, and contract flexibility for quarterly scaling.

Could your team fill the technical portion (GPU mix recommendations, throughput per-GPU, prefix caching assumptions, and a sample commitment plan with cost sensitivity across 6/12/24 month terms)? Also flag any compliance constraints for Aurora's EU customers.

Best,
Maria
Director, Platform Engineering
Aurora Analytics

Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated GPU capacity - initial questionnaire

Maria — thanks for the clear baseline. We reviewed the questionnaire and prepared the attached workbook with: 1) GPU footprint recommendations, 2) throughput estimates by model and batch profile, 3) burst lane design, and 4) three commitment scenarios (6/12/24mo) including burst credits and scaling actions. Highlights up front:

- Recommended steady-state mix: 8x H100 80GB equiv (for your 1.2k-token avg) to hit ~32 sustained req/s with 95th pct tail <120ms for our redwood-3b-quant variant.
- Burst strategy: a reserved burst pool (additional 4x A100-40GB equiv) that can be spun up for up to 10 minutes to absorb 150 req/s spikes, coupled with automatic short-term overprovision credits.
- Caching/Batching assumptions: prefix caching for repeated contexts, request-level batching up to 8 tokens per step, and KV cache warmup for conversational flows — we included sensitivity +/-20% in the workbook.

We've left commentary throughout the workbook about model tradeoffs (H100s give better tail latency; A100s are cost-efficient for short bursts). Rishi added notes on kernel fitment and quantization caveats for long-context models.

I propose a 30-minute call next week to walk through the workbook and align on the commitment options you prefer. When are you available?

—Stephanie
Steph Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated GPU capacity - initial questionnaire

Maria — quick answers to the items you called out:

1) 99th pct throughput: for the recommended H100 mix, expect sustained 99th pct ~25 req/s (per-cluster view) — we've added a per-GPU breakdown in the workbook that shows headroom and queuing at 99th pct. The workbook also includes a column with conservative tail estimates (no caching).

2) Burst pool spin-up: our Dedicated offering uses warm standby containers and pre-warmed AMIs depending on customer policy. For A100-40GB equiv we target sub-90s cold-start (worst-case) and ~20–35s for warm standby activation. We included autoscaler settings that prefer warm standby for critical endpoints and cold spin-up for lower-priority lanes.

3) Per-region mins: commitment scenarios are region-aware. Option A (12mo standard) guarantees minimum 2 full GPUs per region (us/eu/apac) with a pooled global buffer. Option B (24mo) can lock a larger per-region floor with better pricing. Details are in the commitment sheet (tab: "per-region floors").

Note on quantization: if you plan to run LLMs beyond 8k context, H100s provide better memory headroom; for 4k contexts the A100 mix is very cost efficient.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
